title: Integer-base fibred-groupoid limit preservation and versality
statement: Fix the scheme universe and category universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], represented in that universe by $\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{ULift}\mathbf Z)$. Each scheme has its unique structure morphism to $S$, and each scheme map has its corresponding map over $S$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Write $\mathcal F(T)$ for the actual fibre category, and for $a:T\to U$, $x\in\mathcal F(T)$ and $y\in\mathcal F(U)$ write $\operatorname{Lift}(a,x,y)$ for the arrows $x\to y$ in the total category lying over exactly $a$. Limit preservation over this integer base is the specialization of [def-sfb-fibred-groupoid-limit-preserving]: for every nonempty small directed inverse system of affine schemes with affine limit, objects descend to a stage, arrows between pulled-back stage objects descend to a common later stage with their specified identifications, and equality of stage arrows at the limit holds at a later stage. These three predicates are denoted ObjectsDescend, ArrowsDescend and ArrowEqualitiesDescend, and their conjunction is IsLimitPreserving. A point $u\in U$ is a finite type point if its canonical residue-field morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ [def-weil-residue-field] is locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $U$ locally of finite type over $S$ and $x\in\mathcal F(U)$, say $x$ is versal at $u$ if the following lifting condition holds. For all surjections $g:A'\to A$ of Artinian local rings with nilpotent kernel and residue fields identified with $\kappa(u)$, with compatible surjective residue maps having the maximal ideals as kernels, every $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to the canonical morphism from $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ and every $y'\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A')$ with a specified isomorphism $y'|_A\cong a^*x$ admit a lift $a':\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism $y'\cong(a')^*x$ inducing exactly the specified one. Here Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize, and the maps respect the residue-field identifications. Openness of versality means that for every such $U,x$ and every finite type point $u_0$ where $x$ is versal, there is an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $u_0$ such that $x$ is versal at every finite type point of $V$.
